items.acceptedOptionText: Project each station with its active-reservation count.

visibleFacts.prompt: In fleet charging coordinator, The capacity screen lists 40 stations and shows each station’s active reservation count. The operator never opens reservation records from this screen. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The list needs counts only, not reservation objects.
The operator never opens reservation records from the capacity screen.
The capacity-screen read path has a two-query and 1 MB transfer budget; all reservation rows for these stations total 80 MB.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load every reservation for all 40 stations and count them in the screen.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The full reservation rows total 80 MB, far above the screen’s 1 MB transfer budget.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Lazy-load reservations as each count is rendered.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Per-row lazy reads exceed the two-query budget for the screen.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load all station, reservation, charger, and maintenance relationships into one graph.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Loading the reservation graph exceeds the stated 1 MB transfer budget and adds unrelated relationships.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Issue a separate count query for every station after fetching the station page.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: One count query per station exceeds the two-query budget.

items.reason: A scalar count is the consumed information; transferring reservation objects adds data this response never uses. Because reservation details are never opened here, the row can show its count without transferring child records.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A read projection can calculate an aggregate without materializing the related entities.
details.scenarioApplication: The count projection stays within the 1 MB and two-query limits; materializing the reservation graph or issuing one query per station does not.
details.errorCorrection: Loading the full reservation rows sends 80 MB through a path capped at 1 MB; per-station reads also exceed the two-query budget.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If operators could inspect individual reservations inline, a bounded detail load for the selected station would be warranted.
details.transfer: Match the query shape to fields the caller consumes; do not fetch a relationship merely because it exists.

items.acceptedOptionText: Fetch the selected principal and active grants with expiries in one related-data read.

visibleFacts.prompt: In permissions review service, A principal detail view needs active role grants and their expiry dates, but only for the selected principal and at most 10 active grants. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The selected principal has a bounded active-grant set and every expiry is displayed.
This detail request permits at most two database reads for the selected principal.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Lazy-load grants one at a time as the access screen checks each permission.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Per-grant loads repeat access for each displayed permission.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load every role grant and audit event for all principals.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Other principals and complete audit histories are outside this view.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Fetch role names only and make the screen query expiry separately for each grant.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: A second lookup per grant adds hidden round trips for a field already required.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load active grants for every principal, then filter to the selected principal in the screen.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The relationship query should be scoped before transfer to the selected principal.

items.reason: The detail request shows a bounded set for one principal; unrelated grants and principals do not affect it. The response contains active grant expiries for one selected principal within its two-read budget.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A selected-principal boundary limits which grants and expiry values the query needs.
details.scenarioApplication: Only that principal’s at-most-ten active grants appear in the detail response.
details.errorCorrection: Per-grant loads repeat access for each displayed permission.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the grant count were unbounded, paginate the grant view instead of loading all rows.
details.transfer: Scope relationship loading to the selected entity and the exact fields the caller uses.

items.acceptedOptionText: Project component count and current price; load components for the opened bundle.

visibleFacts.prompt: In subscription packaging service, A catalog search returns bundles with component count and current price. Components are shown only after a bundle is opened. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The search shows a summary; component detail is a separate user action.
Components are shown only after a bundle is opened.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load every component for every matching bundle before returning search results.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Fetching all components increases list work for results never opened.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Create a lazy component proxy for every search row and let the UI inspect it.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The UI would own hidden relationship reads.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Read all bundle components to compute prices in the client.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The client should not reconstruct catalog price from component rows when price is a domain value.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load all components to compute the component count, then return only the count.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The query can return the count without transferring every component.

items.reason: A catalog summary can answer search without loading components the user has not opened. Component detail becomes relevant only after the user opens one bundle.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Summary reads can aggregate component information before any component collection is needed.
details.scenarioApplication: Search returns bundle count and price; component records wait for bundle selection.
details.errorCorrection: Fetching all components increases list work for results never opened.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the search displayed component names, project those names or load a bounded summary for the result page.
details.transfer: Separate catalog summaries from component detail when the actual access paths differ.

items.acceptedOptionText: Project revision number and seal time; download bytes only for the selected revision.

visibleFacts.prompt: In document notarization service, A notary searches sealed revisions by document ID and displays each immutable revision number and seal time. The binary document is downloaded only after a row is selected. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The list uses metadata, and bytes are fetched only for the selected immutable revision.
The binary document is downloaded after a row is selected.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load all revision bytes for every matching document into the search result.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Large payloads are not needed for metadata search.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Lazy-load document bytes when each row’s revision number is rendered.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The renderer should not trigger payload reads to show metadata.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load the latest document bytes instead of the exact sealed revision.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The latest revision can differ from the sealed one.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Download each revision file to read its number and seal time.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Those values are metadata; the binary is only needed after row selection.

items.reason: Revision metadata answers the search; the binary is needed only for a selected row. Revision number and seal time identify each result row before any binary download.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Metadata can identify a revision without transferring its content bytes.
details.scenarioApplication: The row displays revision number and seal time; bytes download only after selection.
details.errorCorrection: Large payloads are not needed for metadata search.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the search needed a digest, project the digest field rather than loading the binary content.
details.transfer: Keep metadata lookup and large payload retrieval as separate query shapes when only selected rows need bytes.

items.acceptedOptionText: Group payout rows by seller and settlement window for dashboard totals.

visibleFacts.prompt: In marketplace payout service, The payout dashboard lists seller totals by settlement window. Opening a seller shows the individual payout rows; the dashboard does not need order details. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The summary needs totals, while row details are only used after seller selection.
Order details are not displayed on the dashboard.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load every payout and order for all sellers, then group in the dashboard.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The dashboard need not transfer all underlying records.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Expose lazy payout and order collections to the dashboard and group while rendering.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Lazy traversal still reads every payout and hides query count in the renderer.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Return one generic full graph for both the list and detail screens.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The list and detail contracts consume materially different data.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load all payout rows for the dashboard and calculate seller totals in the UI.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The dashboard needs aggregates and can use a grouped summary query.

items.reason: Totals are the dashboard output; individual payout rows are only needed in seller detail. The dashboard can report settlement-window totals without materializing seller payout details.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Grouped totals answer a summary caller without materializing the detail rows behind them.
details.scenarioApplication: Settlement-window totals appear on the dashboard; payout rows stay in seller detail.
details.errorCorrection: The dashboard need not transfer all underlying records.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the total were calculated from a domain rule not expressible as an aggregate, use an explicitly scoped domain query.
details.transfer: Let query ownership follow whether the caller needs aggregate values or individual domain records.

items.acceptedOptionText: Read current balance and the 12-row recent allocation page; leave older history to search.

visibleFacts.prompt: In cooperative lending ledger, A repayment screen opens one account, displays its current balance and 12 recent allocations, and can record a new allocation before leaving the account transaction. Older allocations are available through a separate history search. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The operation needs one account and a bounded recent page; historical search is separate.
Older allocations are available through a separate history search.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Eager-load the account’s entire lifetime allocation history.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: The entire history is not consumed by this operation.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Use a lazy allocation collection and let each screen action issue reads as needed.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Unplanned lazy access makes the transaction’s read set unclear.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Load the complete borrower, all accounts, and every allocation to calculate the balance.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: Unrelated accounts and borrower records are outside the selected account operation.

wrongOptionDiagnostics.optionText: Keep the full lifetime allocation collection attached to the account for this screen.
wrongOptionDiagnostics.feedback: This operation needs only the recent page and current balance; the full history is a separate search.

items.reason: The operation needs a bounded recent page and current balance; older allocations have a separate search path. The recent allocation page and balance support this account operation while lifetime history stays separate.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A bounded recent page and a separate history query serve different read scopes.
details.scenarioApplication: The account operation uses balance plus 12 recent allocations, not lifetime history.
details.errorCorrection: The entire history is not consumed by this operation.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the balance must be recomputed from all allocations, that becomes an explicit aggregate requirement rather than an implicit graph load.
details.transfer: Define the operation’s read set and bounds before choosing how relationships are loaded.
